To address the issue you're experiencing with Open WebUI, you should follow these steps to check and verify the fix:

### Step 1: Check Configuration Changes
Ensure that the configuration changes related to this behavior have been correctly implemented. Specifically, look for changes in the codebase that handle model visibility in the admin Models list. The changes should reflect that disabled models are kept visible for the purpose of re-enabling them.

### Step 2: Review Documentation
Check if there are any updates in the documentation regarding the behavior of model visibility when they are disabled. Documentation might provide insights into how the feature works and how to properly manage it.

### Step 3: Verify Code Implementation
Review the relevant code files (likely in the admin area of the WebUI application) that handle the state of models being disabled or enabled. Look for changes that prevent models from disappearing when they are disabled.

### Step 4: Test the Behavior
Log into the Open WebUI as an administrator and navigate to the Models list in the admin section. Disable a model and observe whether it remains visible in the list. You should also be able to re-enable the model from the same list.

### Step 5: Confirm Reversibility
After disabling a model and ensuring it stays visible, try re-enabling it and confirm that the model’s status updates accordingly. This will help verify that the feature works as intended, allowing you to recover a disabled model without it vanishing from the list.

### Step 6: Check for Additional Issues
While testing, keep an eye out for any other unexpected behavior or issues that may arise when disabling or re-enabling models. This will help ensure that the fix does not introduce other problems.

### Step 7: Report Back
After completing the above steps, report back with your findings. If everything works as expected, it indicates that the fix is correctly implemented. If you encounter any issues, document them clearly so that they can be addressed in a subsequent update.

By following these steps, you can effectively check and verify the fix for the behavior of disabled models in the Open WebUI.
